tip: wedi before a verb marks the perfect: Dw i wedi pasio = I have passed. Replace wedi with yn for I am passing.
An Oedd form plus wedi is the past perfect: Oeddech chi wedi gorffen? = Had you finished?, one step back from the plain past.
erbyn marks a deadline, not a moment: erbyn wyth o'r gloch = by eight o'clock, meaning done before then.
newydd plus a softened verb means just did: newydd gyrraedd (from cyrraedd) = has just arrived. Use wedi for the plain perfect.
eisoes means already and sits just before wedi: mae e eisoes wedi pacio = he has already packed.
In a negative, erioed means never in all past time: Dyw e erioed wedi bod = he has never been.
Byddai plus wedi bod is would have been: Byddai hi wedi bod yn braf = it would have been nice.
heb is the not-done counterpart of wedi: heb symud = not having moved, where wedi symud would mean having moved.
wedi'i plus a softened verb says it has been done to the thing: wedi'i ferwi (from berwi) = boiled.
For plural things use wedi'u, adding h before a vowel: wedi'u hanfon (from anfon) = have been sent.
Welsh has no verb to have; it uses gyda: Oes tocyn sbâr gyda ti? = literally is there a spare ticket with you?
The preposition i softens the word after it: i Ddulyn (from Dulyn) = to Dublin.
ers covers a span still going: wedi byw ... ers pymtheng mlynedd = have lived for fifteen years and still do.
Counting years uses blynedd, not blwyddyn, and it nasal-mutates to mlynedd after five: bum mlynedd = five years.
The in word yn becomes yng and nasal-mutates a place name: Ceredigion turns into yng Ngheredigion.
A feminine noun softens its adjective: awyr is feminine, so glas becomes awyr las = blue sky.
The -wyd ending is an agentless passive: Gwrthodwyd y pryd = the meal was sent back, with no doer named.
Reported clauses use bod, softened to fod, for that: Cyfaddefodd e fod e wedi gwneud = he admitted that he had made.
nag means than before a vowel (na before a consonant): yn fwynach nag arfer = milder than usual.
The -odd ending is the he/she past for one finished event: Methodd = he failed, pasiodd = he passed.
'n lân, literally clean, works as an intensifier meaning completely: wedi blino'n lân = worn out.
cwrdd takes â to mean meet with: cwrdd â chi = meet you. â here is with.
o'r blaen means before now and pairs with the perfect: wedi bod yma o'r blaen = have been here before.
